description.value: This fMRI study examined how short-term cognitive reappraisal, suppression, and up-regulation strategies modulate food craving and mesocorticolimbic BOLD activity in healthy women.

value: cognitive reappraisal would most effectively inhibit the mesocorticolimbic activity and associated food craving as compared to suppression
suppression would lead to more prefrontal cortex activity, reflecting the use of more control resources, as compared to cognitive reappraisal
self-reported food cravings would be higher following the up-regulation strategy, as compared to suppression and cognitive reappraisal

source_definition.value: Cognitive control strategy with levels cognitive reappraisal, suppression, and up-regulation; the strategies were applied while viewing palatable food pictures.

spans.text: Participants were instructed to look at palatable food pictures and 1) imagine the food's palatable smell, texture and taste (i.e., up-regulation), 2) immediately inhibit any thoughts concerning food palatability and/or food cravings (i.e., suppression), or 3) focus on alternative meanings of the presented food cues, for example, the longer term consequences of consuming the food for their health (i.e., cognitive reappraisal).

description.value: Functional images were preprocessed with slice scan timing correction, motion correction, high-pass filtering, smoothing, and spatial normalization.

spans.text: Preprocessing comprised slice scan timing correction (using sinc interpolation), motion correction (using a 3D rigid-body transformation of each volume to the first volume of each run and using sinc interpolation) and high-pass filtering to remove low-frequency noise (up to 3 cycles in the single run time-course). Individual functional data were smoothed using a 6 mm full-width-at-half-maximum isotropic Gaussian Kernel. The anatomical scan and the functional data were then spatially normalized using Talairach transformation procedures ( ).

Participants viewed palatable food pictures while applying cognitive reappraisal, suppression, up-regulation, or passive viewing strategies.

spans.text: Participants were instructed to look at palatable food pictures and 1) imagine the food's palatable smell, texture and taste (i.e., up-regulation), 2) immediately inhibit any thoughts concerning food palatability and/or food cravings (i.e., suppression), or 3) focus on alternative meanings of the presented food cues, for example, the longer term consequences of consuming the food for their health (i.e., cognitive reappraisal).

The stop sign indicated that the participant should look at the presented food cue in a neutral way and immediately inhibit any thoughts ( ) or cravings, which can also be behavioral, ( ) related to the palatability of the presented food, without looking away from the picture (i.e., suppression).
